subject: Private deployment network readiness & performance next steps
messages:
From: Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.com>
To: Ethan Coleman <ethan.coleman@calderahealth.com>
Cc: Lisa Hsu <lisa.hsu@calderahealth.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>, Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-04-10T14:08:00-07:00
Subject: Private deployment network readiness & performance next steps

Thanks for taking the call today — great discussion. I wanted to recap the agreed performance targets and list concrete next steps so we can move the private deployment qualification forward. Summary of targets you confirmed on the call:
- Latency SLO: p95 end-to-end inference < 80 ms for 512-token prompts (regional to VPC egress to Redwood cluster)
- Throughput: sustained 2.5–3.0 Gbps of egress for peak batch windows (expected sustained inference traffic at peak)
- Concurrency: 600 simultaneous streaming sessions (average message size ~1.2 KB) with graceful degradation above that
- Streaming: require token-level streaming (partial tokens) to the client; client must accept out-of-order partial frames if backpressure occurs

Network path notes we discussed: you prefer VPN+BGP failover initially with a plan to migrate to cloud peering within 60 days. Key verification items: MTU sizing (1500 vs jumbo), NAT/port preservation for long-lived streams, whether TLS termination will be inside Caldera or Redwood, and whether there are intermediate firewalls doing deep packet inspection.

Action items (owner / ETA):
1) Caldera ops to provide VPN endpoint details, IP blocks, and egress gateway NAT behavior (Ethan / by 2027-04-12)
2) Redwood infra to provide IP ranges, TLS cipher requirements, and expected test addresses for iperf/traceroute (Vivek / by 2027-04-11)
3) Joint test window: 2-hour connectivity + throughput window + synthetic p95 latency runs (mutually agreed; target week of 2027-04-19) (Priya coordinate)
4) Exchange of the short network checklist & mutual action plan (attached) (Priya / today)

I attached a concise network checklist and a draft mutual action plan to make the prep work lighter. If anything above is incorrect or missing, flag it and I’ll update the plan.

Thanks — Priya
Priya Natarajan

Subject: Re: Private deployment network readiness & performance next steps

Thanks Priya — that matches our notes and is very helpful. A few clarifications from our side before we hand over firewall/VPN configs:
1) Latency: 80 ms p95 is our goal, but we need to understand how MTU changes and TLS termination could shift that. Can Redwood provide an expected delta table (e.g., baseline p95 on private link vs TLS terminated at Redwood)?
2) Streaming: our client SDK currently expects an in-order stream; we can accept partial frames but would prefer server-side buffering for reordering if possible. Is that supported?
3) Throughput: our infra team estimates conservative 2 Gbps but we can scale to 3 Gbps during peaks. Will Redwood autoscale for short peak bursts, or do we need reserved capacity?

I’ll gather the VPN endpoint details and the NAT behavior doc and send them by EOD Monday (2027-04-12). Also looping Lisa (network lead) for questions on MTU and firewall behaviors.

—Ethan
Ethan Coleman
Senior Infrastructure Engineer, Caldera Health

Date: 2027-04-11T09:15:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Private deployment network readiness & performance next steps

Ethan — good questions. Short answers first, then technical attachments below:
- Latency delta: in our experience TLS termination inside Redwood vs at-customer is ~8–18 ms p95 depending on region and crypto profile; we’ll instrument a short test and share expected deltas for your specific route.
- Streaming reordering: Redwood supports token-level streaming with sequence numbers; we can enable a lightweight server-side reordering buffer (configurable up to 250 ms) if you prefer in-order delivery. That will slightly increase p95, we’ll provide a trade-off table.
- Bursts vs reserved capacity: for bursts under 10 minutes we rely on autoscaling and our burst pool; for predictable sustained peaks above 2.5 Gbps we recommend a short Dedicated capacity reservation to guarantee throughput and avoid cold-start tails.

I’ve uploaded two short artifacts (attached): network checklist (iperf/traceroute test steps, expected ports, sample iperf flags) and a suggested test script for measuring token-level latency under streaming. Vivek / Dylan — see the checklist and confirm whether the 250 ms reordering buffer option looks safe for our current runtime and whether it introduces additional memory/CPU overhead during peak concurrency.

Proposed test schedule: 2027-04-20 01:00–03:00 UTC (we can shift earlier/later — please confirm)

Thanks — Priya

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>

Date: 2027-04-11T11:42:00-07:00
Subject: RE: Private deployment network readiness & performance next steps (tech notes)

Quick tech notes for the internal team (copying here to keep a single thread):
- Reordering buffer: 250 ms configurable buffer is fine; expect ~3–6% increase in p95 for token-size bursts. Memory overhead: ~12 MB per 1k concurrent streams (manageable for their expected 600 concurrency).
- MTU: ask Caldera to test with both 1500 and 9000 if their on-prem path supports jumbo frames; jumbo gives measurable throughput gains for large batch transfers but less impact on small streaming packets.
- NAT/Keepalive: long-lived TLS streams require NAT idle timeout > 15 minutes or periodic TCP keepalives from client. Recommend we include keepalive guidance in the checklist.
- iperf: use iperf3 with -P 16 and -w 256k for throughput baseline; run both UDP and TCP tests to check packet loss affecting p95.

Next steps for internal owners:
* Dylan: prepare a short script that will run token-level synthetic loads during the test window and emit p50/p95/p99 reports (due 2027-04-18).
* Marissa: validate the peering vs VPN test plan and list fallbacks for BGP flaps (due 2027-04-16).

Vivek
Principal Infra Engineer, Redwood Inference
